newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends firmer but gains pared.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends firmer but gains pared.

text.p: Despite another sharp drawdown in LME stocks on Tuesday which initially helped boost the market, most of the gains were disappointingly lost by close of trade as follow through support failed to appear, traders and analysts said.
LME stocks tumbled by a larger-than-expected 10,950 tonnes to 191,550 tonnes, below a month's global consumption.
But several analysts have said much of the metal is probably being stockpiled in warehouses in China and not being consumed.
"The change in the spreads from this wide backwardation that we had has certainly been responsible for some of the stock movements," said William O'Neill of Merrill Lynch.
Traders said much metal was lent into the market to capture the strong backwardation which, in recent weeks switched into a brief contango before returning to a modest backwardation once more.

"Possibly we could start to see some of the material start to come back into the market as we near the end of this month and go into November. I don't think that the current trend of stock declines is going to continue," O'Neill said.
December COMEX settled 0.50 cent firmer at 90.60 cents a lb, traded 92.20 to 90.40 cents. Spot October went out 0.40 cent firmer at 91.90 cents.
LME three-months continues to hit resistance in the $1,970 to $1,980 per tonne area, with even large stock drawdowns failing to generate enough follow through to make a decisive upside move.
One LME and COMEX broker said influential shorts were selling on the highs to abort any upside breakout in a market whose short-term fundamentals were bullish.

U.S. demand remains strong and copper scrap is in short supply on both sides of the Atlantic. However, if the General Motors strike in Canada and resulting lay offs in the U.S. become protracted, copper scrap and eventually rod demand may be affected, merchants said.
The CFTC Commitment of Traders report for week ended October 8, released Monday, showed that speculators have become more long in COMEX copper futures while the trade remained heavily short.
Speculators held 9,271 long and 6,260 short positions, while the commercials held 38,861 short positions and 24,787 long positions.
LME stocks in Long Beach fell by almost three thousand tonnes, but brokers said there were still delays of over a month in taking metal out.
